title: Mixtures and Separation Techniques
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Mixtures and Separation Techniques Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Mixtures are combinations of substances that can be separated by physical methods such as picking, sieving, filtering, decanting, evaporation, magnetic separation and distillation. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 6, Quarter 1: Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Materials): pure substances and mixtures, kinds of mixtures, separating mixtures, separation methods and separation in industry and the environment. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mixtures can be separated by physical methods.
body_html:
How to think about it

A pure substance has only one kind of particle; a mixture has two or more. In a heterogeneous mixture you can see the different parts, like gravel and sand or oil and water.

Mixtures are separated by differences in their parts: sieving and filtering use particle size, settling and flotation use density, and a magnet pulls out iron. Mines use these methods to separate valuable minerals from rock.

Example

How can you separate sand from water?

Sand particles are bigger than the holes in paper.

Answer: filter it

Example

Oil floats on water. Which property separates them?

Which one is less dense?

Answer: density

Common mistakes

  • Thinking you can filter out dissolved salt.
  • Calling salt water a heterogeneous mixture (it is a solution).
  • Forgetting that a magnet only picks up iron, nickel and cobalt.

items.q: 50 mL of water and 50 mL of rubbing alcohol are mixed. The total is less than 100 mL. Why?
c: Small particles fit into the spaces between larger ones.
items.e: This supports the particle theory.

items.q: What is a suspension?

items.e: Muddy water and some salad dressings are suspensions.

items.q: Is tap water a pure substance or a mixture?
items.e: A pure substance contains only one kind of particle; a mixture contains two or more substances not chemically joined.

items.q: What does the particle theory say about particles of matter?
c: They are always moving and have spaces between them.
They are the same in every substance.

items.q: What is a pure substance?

a mix of two or more substances

items.q: Why is it important to know if a product is a mixture?
c: The parts may be separated and some may be harmful or recyclable.
items.e: Labels list the parts of a mixture.

items.q: Which is a compound?
items.e: Compounds have two or more kinds of atoms joined together.

items.q: When oil paint dissolves in turpentine to make thinned paint, what is the solvent?
items.e: The solute dissolves; the solvent does the dissolving; together they make the solution.

items.q: Which method separates an insoluble solid from a liquid?

items.e: Use evaporating because sugar is dissolved.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by filtration?
c: the different dyes in a black ink
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by chromatography?
c: the colors in a food coloring
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sea water (to get the salt)?
items.e: Use evaporating because salt is dissolved in sea water.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate rice and flour?
items.e: Use sieving because the flour is fine enough to pass through.

items.q: Which method is best for separating iron filings and sand?
items.e: Iron is magnetic; sand is not.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by distillation?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which method separates sand from water?
items.e: The filter traps the sand.

items.q: What is distillation?
c: boiling a liquid and condensing the vapor to collect a pure liquid
items.e: Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate salt from salt water?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which method is best for separating steel cans and aluminum cans at a recycling plant?
items.e: Steel is attracted to a magnet; aluminum is not.

items.q: Which method is best for separating tea leaves and tea?
items.e: The tea leaves are the residue.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate gravel and sand?
items.e: Use sieving because the gravel pieces are bigger than the holes.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sand and water?
items.e: Use filtering because sand is insoluble and is caught by the filter paper.

items.q: Which method is best for separating pure water from ink?
items.e: The water is collected as the distillate.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate muddy water?
items.e: Use filtering because mud is made of insoluble bits.

items.q: What does soluble mean?
c: able to dissolve in a solvent
items.e: Salt is soluble in water.

items.q: Why does a sieve separate gravel from sand?
c: The holes let small sand grains through but stop larger gravel.
items.e: Sieving uses particle size.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate iron filings and sand?
items.e: Use using a magnet because iron is magnetic; sand is not.

items.q: Which method separates the inks in a marker?
items.e: Each ink travels up the paper at a different speed.

items.q: Which method is best for separating salt from salt solution?
items.e: The water evaporates and leaves the salt behind.

items.q: What is the principle behind distillation?
c: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapor is cooled and condensed.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how distillation works.

items.q: Which method is best for separating the dyes in a black marker ink?
items.e: The dyes move different distances up the paper.

items.q: Kristine dissolves 25 g of salt in 150 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: What is the filtrate?
c: the liquid that passes through the filter paper
the solid left on the filter paper
items.e: The solid left behind is the residue.

items.q: Diane mixes 8 g of sand with 50 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Nico dissolves 20 g of salt in 150 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Which step is a good first step?
c: Add water and stir so the salt dissolves.
Evaporate the water to get the salt back.
Use a magnet to remove the iron filings.
items.e: Take out the magnetic iron first, while everything is dry.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Why is water added and stirred before filtering?
c: so the salt dissolves and passes through the filter, leaving the sand
items.e: Only the dissolved salt goes through the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains gravel, iron filings and salt. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: Which method is best for separating the colorings in a sweet?
items.e: Each coloring travels at its own rate.

items.q: Bianca mixes 12 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: How can chromatography help to keep food safe?
c: It can show whether a food contains a banned coloring.
items.e: The spots are compared with known dyes.

items.q: Christian dissolves 5 g of salt in 100 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Which method is best for separating pure water from orange juice?
items.e: Only the water boils off and is condensed.

items.q: Vincent mixes 10 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Which separation technique works on this principle? Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how paper chromatography works.

items.q: Kenneth dissolves 8 g of salt in 150 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Rose mixes 5 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?

sets.title: Separation in industry and the environment

items.q: A recycling plant uses a large magnet on a moving belt. What does it remove?
items.e: Steel contains iron, which is magnetic.

items.q: Ethanol boils at 78 °C and water at 100 °C. A mixture of the two is heated. Which liquid is collected first?
items.e: The liquid with the lower boiling point boils off first.

items.q: Rose dissolves 10 g of salt in 200 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: What is the best way to separate sand and water?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: The filter paper lets water through but stops the sand grains.

items.q: Which method separates iron filings and sand?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Iron is attracted to a magnet; sand is not.

items.q: What is a solvent?
c: the substance that does the dissolving
items.e: Water is called the universal solvent.

items.q: What is concentration?
c: the amount of solute in a certain amount of solution
items.e: More solute means higher concentration.

items.q: A solution has 20 g of salt in 100 mL of water. What is its concentration?
What is the best way to separate steel paper clips and rice?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
add water and skim off what floats
items.e: The steel clips are attracted to a magnet; rice is not.

items.q: What is a solute?
c: a solid that does not dissolve
the substance that does the dissolving
items.e: Sugar is the solute in sugar water.

items.q: Which method separates wood chips and sand?
c: add water and skim off what floats
items.e: Wood floats in water and sand sinks, so the wood chips can be skimmed off.

items.q: Which would dissolve sugar fastest?
c: cold water, not stirred, with sugar cubes
hot water, stirred, with fine sugar
items.e: Heat, stirring and smaller pieces speed up dissolving.

items.q: How do recycling plants separate steel cans from aluminum cans?
items.e: Steel is magnetic; aluminum is not.

items.q: Angelo mixes 25 g of sand with 200 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: How are oil spills cleaned up on water?
c: with floating booms and skimmers, because oil floats on water
items.e: Oil and water do not mix.

items.q: What is a saturated solution?
c: a mixture of sand and water
a solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature
items.e: Extra solute sinks to the bottom.

items.q: A student heats copper(II) sulfate solution until it is dry. Why might she stop before it is completely dry?
c: To get crystals instead of a powder that may decompose with too much heat.
To make it a liquid again.
items.e: Heat gently and let crystals form as it cools.

items.q: Why must the solvent level be below the start line in paper chromatography?
c: So that the dyes move faster.
So that the paper does not get wet.
So that the dyes do not dissolve straight into the solvent in the beaker.
items.e: The solvent must carry the dyes up the paper.

items.q: Which method separates iron filings from sulfur powder?
items.e: Iron is magnetic.

items.q: Which method separates oil and water?
c: let it settle and pour off the top layer
items.e: Oil does not dissolve in water; it floats as a layer on top that can be poured or scooped off.
